bibliographic.title: VOYAGER: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
bibliographic.authors: Guanzhi Wang, Yuqi Xie, Yunfan Jiang, Ajay Mandlekar, Chaowei Xiao, Yuke Zhu, Linxi Jim Fan, Anima Anandkumar
bibliographic.citation_apa: Wang, G., Xie, Y., Jiang, Y., Mandlekar, A., Xiao, C., Zhu, Y., Fan, L., & Anandkumar, A. (2023). VOYAGER: An open-ended embodied agent with large language models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2305.16291.

methodology.method_family: LLM-based embodied agent with automatic curriculum, skill library, and iterative prompting evaluated in Minecraft simulation
methodology.study_design: Experimental technical evaluation against LLM-agent baselines in MineDojo/Minecraft
methodology.sample_description: Minecraft open-ended environment; comparisons with LLM-based agent techniques such as ReAct, Reflexion, and AutoGPT
methodology.technology_context: Embodied lifelong-learning agent using GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 via blackbox prompting in Minecraft; code-as-action space with environment feedback and self-verification

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The study addresses embodied autonomous LLM agents for open-ended Minecraft exploration and skill acquisition, not conversational governance, compliance, auditability, human oversight, or regulated high-stakes deployment contexts.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the paper is strongly LLM-specific and describes agent architecture with logs, errors, and interpretable skills, its central focus is autonomous embodied learning without human intervention in a game environment. The provided text contains no substantive treatment of conversational governance, guardrails, compliance, accountability, contestation, or regulated-domain application.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Scope mismatch is explicit in the abstract and introduction; exclusion does not depend on ambiguous terminology matching.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal reflects only the provided front matter and excerpts. The study appears methodologically coherent for embodied-agent benchmarking, but ethics, limitations, and full evaluation protocol are not visible in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: Internal coherence and empirical support appear adequate for embodied-agent claims in Minecraft, but relevance to conversational governance in regulated LLM systems is very low based on the provided text.

coding.subtheme: Open-ended skill discovery in simulated game environments

synthesis.main_claim: VOYAGER is an LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent in Minecraft that autonomously explores, acquires reusable skills, and outperforms prior LLM-agent baselines on exploration and task-progress metrics.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes a three-component architecture—automatic curriculum, growing skill library, and iterative prompting with environment feedback, execution errors, and self-verification—for open-ended embodied learning using GPT-4 without fine-tuning.
synthesis.limitations: Provided excerpts do not report study limitations, ethics, or governance implications; evaluation context is limited to Minecraft/MineDojo rather than regulated conversational systems.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central or supporting evidence on conversational governance in regulated LLM systems; at most brief contextual mention as an example of autonomous LLM-agent architecture outside governed conversational deployment.
